DETAILED ACTION
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 102
The following is a quotation of the appropriate paragraphs of 35 U.S.C. 102 that form the basis for the rejections under this section made in this Office action:
A person shall be entitled to a patent unless –
(a)(1) the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
(a)(2) the claimed invention was described in a patent issued under section 151, or in an application for patent published or deemed published under section 122(b), in which the patent or application, as the case may be, names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
Claim(s) 1-20 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102a1 as being anticipated by Buckland (U.S. Pat. NO. 10,895,197).
Regarding claims 1, 9 and 17, Buckland discloses a computer-implemented (14 is the computer with 16 being the sensors and 81 being the actuators) method that, when executed by data processing hardware of a motor vehicle including a turbocharger having a turbine, causes the data processing hardware to perform operations comprising:
receiving an accelerator pedal position input indicating that a vehicle accelerator pedal has moved to an overrun position (206 and 208.  Tip-in is acceleration and tip-out is construed as the overrun position);
receiving one or more vehicle performance parameter inputs each corresponding to a measured vehicle performance parameter (the accelerator pedal position is a performance parameter, claim 7 of this application also states this);
calculating a vehicle dynamic score (construed as a determination of accelerating, slowing, or maintaining) based on the one or more vehicle performance parameter inputs (206 and 208);
Note: as per applicants specification ¶46 this is simply a determination that the vehicle is in a “dynamic operating state” which will be understood as not being in steady state.
determining a target boost profile based on the calculated vehicle dynamic score (210 is determining current boost conditions in comparison to desired); and
instructing one or more outputs of the vehicle to transition to a dynamic mode to generate an increased turbine power based on the target boost profile (212).
Regarding claim 2, 10 and 18 which depends from claim 1, 9 and 17 respectively, Buckland discloses further comprising: determining that the vehicle is in a dynamic state when the calculated vehicle dynamic score exceeds a threshold vehicle dynamic score (206 and 208); and when the vehicle is in the dynamic state, instructing the one or more outputs of the vehicle to transition to the dynamic mode to generate the increased turbine power (212).
Regarding claim 3, 11 and 19 which depends from claim 1, 9 and 17 respectively, Buckland discloses wherein the one or more vehicle performance parameter inputs includes at least one of a vehicle acceleration input or an accelerator pedal position (pedal position option addressed with 206, 208).
Regarding claim 4, 12 and 20 which depends from claim 1, 9 and 17 respectively, Buckland discloses wherein determining that the vehicle is in a dynamic state includes determining that the vehicle is the dynamic state while the accelerator pedal is in the overrun position (208).
Regarding claim 5 and 13 which depends from claim 1 and 9 respectively, Buckland discloses wherein the one or more outputs of the vehicle include an air intake rate (wastegate option addressed), a fuel intake rate (wastegate option addressed), a wastegate actuator output (212 adjusts the wastegate), and a camshaft phaser output (wastegate option addressed).
Regarding claim 6 and 14 which depends from claim 1 and 9 respectively, Buckland discloses wherein the operation of instructing one or more outputs of the vehicle to transition to a dynamic mode occurs while the accelerator pedal is in the overrun position (212 is due to 208 which is construed as the overrun position).
Regarding claim 7 and 15 which depends from claim 1 and 9 respectively, Buckland discloses wherein the one or more vehicle performance parameter inputs include accelerator pedal position (addressed above), accelerator pedal position rate of change (position option addressed), and accelerator pedal position accumulation (position option addressed).
Regarding claim 8 and 16 which depends from claim 7 and 15 respectively, Buckland discloses wherein the one or more vehicle performance parameter inputs includes brake pedal position, braking force, vehicle lateral force, vehicle longitudinal force, driver selected vehicle mode, engine speed, vehicle speed, and transmission gear selection (accelerator pedal position option addressed).
Conclusion
The prior art made of record and not relied upon is considered pertinent to applicant's disclosure. Please review when considering a response to this office action.
